children: revealed AIForce, which provides a path for businesses to utilize headless software-as-a-service for their artificial intelligence goals, during its Dreamforce event in San Francisco this week.

AIForce is a live interface layer that delivers all the enterprise knowledge inside Salesforce, such as data, workflows, business logic, semantics, permissions, security, and governance, into any AI interface.

Employees who have never opened a Salesforce dashboard can now ask questions, update records, and trigger workflows, all grounded in Salesforce's data and business logic. They can access the data through Anthropic's
Claude, Slack, Lightning, Coworker and other options.

"AI is creating an interface revolution," said Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff. "We are combining model intelligence with all the context that customers have built into Salesforce to create an intelligent, dynamic, composable system that is securely governed, built with Zero Data Retention, and designed to work with the core systems that already run your business."
Financial analysts were positive on the release.

"We believe the company delivered a compelling vision for AIforce during the keynote, with ready-to-try headless capabilities available to customers today, versus prior years when demoed capabilities were not yet ready for production environments," said Stifel analyst J. Parker Lane in an investor note. "Additionally, we think the focus on zero data retention throughout the keynotes resonates with customers, given recent news items that bring into question whether LLMs are retaining conversations or learning from user queries/logic (see: controversy around OpenAI solving Navier-Stokes problem)."
Salesforce also introduced Koa, the company's first CRM reasoning model, which was built on Nvidia's

"The most valuable thing Salesforce has built isn't our platform—it's the accumulated knowledge of how enterprise business actually works," Benioff said. "With Koa, the knowledge is put inside the model itself. We trained a reasoning engine that understands the structure of a deal, the lifecycle of a service case, and the workflows that vary across industries. That's a different kind of intelligence, and it runs entirely inside your trust boundary."

"Nvidia's Nemotron 3 powers Koa and enables an open-source reasoning engine trained on synthetic scenarios, not customer data, fully understanding sales cycles simulating real-world workflows," said KeyBanc analyst Jackson Ader in a note. "Nvidia Nemotron models allow Salesforce to have control to build CRM intelligence into the model itself, controlling the weights coupled with running within CRM infrastructure, ensuring a data trust boundary during inference."
Salesforce also provided some color on the pricing tiers for AIForce.

"Per the keynote, Core subscriptions are priced at $195 per user per month, while Salesforce in Claude is included only in Advanced and Max at list prices of $395 and $550, respectively, with unmetered access to Coworker only accessible through Max," said J.P. Morgan analyst Sammik Chatterjee in a note. "The three tiers Core/Advanced/Max come with Flex Credit allocations of 500K/1M/2.75M and a free upgrade to Max for existing Agentforce 1 customers; per the September 3 packaging announcement, Core and Advanced replace the legacy Enterprise and Unlimited editions, and Max holds the Agentforce 1 price point."

"In our view, the free Agentforce 1 Edition-to-Max upgrade limits near-term uplift at the top of the base, so the watchpoint is the pace of Enterprise/Unlimited renewals migrating to Advanced/Max, where any color at the investor session on uplift will be watched," he added.
During the event, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said enterprises are only beginning to tap into the potential of AI.

"Mr. Amodei stated that currently enterprises are only tapping into 5%-10% of AI potential, and there is headroom to grow simply by broader deployment and workflow integration, not just model advancements," said Truist analyst Terry Tillman in a note. "Mr. Amodei stated that Anthropic's CRO currently uses Claude to tap into Salesforce data daily to review top deals, risks, and win strategies."
